GodLike Esports sweep Trigger Point Esports to stay unbeaten in South Asia Kickoff qualifier

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, godLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier.
  • GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that the playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, godLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 in the upper bracket of the VCT Pacific Kickoff South Asia qualifier. Only two South Asian sides will reach the Last Chance Qualifier, where a single place at Kickoff in Bangkok is on offer.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

Sources indicate that the playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

Recent findings suggest that godLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

In a recent development, south Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a latest organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

It has been revealed that russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

Tech Report: Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

📅 11 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (408 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • It has been revealed that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

It has been revealed that on the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

In a recent development, with the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

Industry observers note that that same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

It has been revealed that and, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The search for secrets in World of Warcraft: Forever continues ever onwards, with a latest breakthrough coming to light in recent days. The latest discovery? An elusive new cat that can be tamed by hunters in one of the game's new zones.

Recent findings suggest that the cat's name is Ta'Shkal, and they can be found on Mount Hyjal. An endgame levelling zone, players will have to reach at least level 57 in order to safely make their way up there and recruit this fresh pet.

Recent findings suggest that the way you do so is relatively simple. You need to find a small corrupted cat figuring within the Felblood Scar region of Mount Hyjal. Once you've found that, you then need to travel up to a hidden lantern south of the Mourning's Rest area. With the figurine in your bags, you'll be able to interact with the lantern, spawning the cat for you to tame (granted you're playing a hunter).

In a recent development, so what's the substantial deal about this cat? Well, aside from the fact it's got a strange colour scheme of green fur with orange stripes, the cat also has a base attack speed of 1.0. This means it'll attack once every second, which is pretty fast and allows for greater damage output from your pet. This inherently makes the pet valuable for endgame hunter players, who are looking to improve their performance in PvE and PvP.

Sources indicate that this is not the only secret discovered by World of Warcraft: Forever sleuths. Last week, they pieced together a hidden quest chain that leads to two special swords. As of writing, only one has been found, though progress continues in pursuit of the second.

It has been revealed that the game has been out for just over two weeks now, and continues to prove popular among new and returning players. It's the biggest launch in the series' history, and has gone down well with people so far. Even if it has recently suffered its first controversy with a now-fixed gold exploit.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While some developers with the studio have been trying for months or even longer to get the initiative off the ground to protect their employee rights, the latest results shared by the IWGB union on Instagram show that there's still a lot more work to be done.
  • According to reports from sources like the Video Games Chronicle, a vast majority of Rockstar employees voted against the deal that would have seen IWGB representing them as the studio's official union, which turned out to be roughly 75%, or about 1,200 out of the 1,600 employees that participated in the vote against it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The industry-shaking release of Grand Theft Auto 6 has overshadowed just about everything else going on in the gaming world right now, but one area that has suffered the most seems to be the efforts of the union trying to form a partnership with Rockstar's employees.

While some developers with the studio have been trying for months or even longer to get the initiative off the ground to protect their employee rights, the latest results shared by the IWGB union on Instagram show that there's still a lot more work to be done.

According to reports from sources like the Video Games Chronicle, a vast majority of Rockstar employees voted against the deal that would have seen IWGB representing them as the studio's official union, which turned out to be roughly 75%, or about 1,200 out of the 1,600 employees that participated in the vote against it.

While IWGB has had plenty of support leading up to the official vote, which ran from November 12 to November 26, several current Rockstar employees have already been expressing exactly why they think the vote failed, or why they voted no in the first place.

With statements like how "many of us had legitimate concerns that couldn't be answered fully by the IWGB" or dozens of others expressing how their "time at Rockstar has been amazing" with some of the "best working conditions I could possibly dream of," the vote had a lot going against it already.

The main problem many Rockstar employees had with the vote wasn't the concept of a union representing and protecting them itself, but more so the IWGB specifically, which several responses pointed out how they "failed to provide any practical advantages" and made several campaign claims that didn't accurately represent what it was actually like to work at Rockstar during the creation of GTA 6.

The timing of the vote couldn't have been worse either, as while the IWGB was using the release of GTA 6 to provide more attention to their initiative, several Rockstar employees have previously stated they didn't want to take away from the efforts of the developers that worked so hard on the project, or wanted to reap the success of the launch rather than put it at risk over more unsteady union conflicts.

Despite the current results of the vote, however, the IWGB Game Workers union isn't giving up on Rockstar by any means, as they are using the smaller portion of success to "double down" on their efforts and individual representation for Rockstar employees who opt into their organization, as opposed to moving the whole workforce into it.

PlayStation creator states it was his "secret intention" to trick Microsoft into making Xbox

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ken Kutaragi led the development of Sony's video game consoles for years, and is widely known as "the father of the PlayStation." As it turns out, he might also be the father of the Xbox – or, at least, its distant uncle.
  • Industry observers note that "I had the chance to meet with the head of Microsoft one-to-one," Kutaragi tells The Game Business.
  • "Sony has no money, but they have huge money," Kutaragi continues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ken Kutaragi led the development of Sony's video game consoles for years, and is widely known as "the father of the PlayStation." As it turns out, he might also be the father of the Xbox – or, at least, its distant uncle. In a new interview, Kutaragi claims to have been playing 4D chess in a meeting with a Microsoft executive, essentially tricking the tech giant into creating its own game console.

Industry observers note that "I had the chance to meet with the head of Microsoft one-to-one," Kutaragi tells The Game Business. The literal head of Microsoft in this era would, of course, have been Bill Gates, though Kutaragi isn't specific about who specifically he spoke to. Whoever it was, he wasn't terribly impressed: "He was so arrogant.".

"Sony has no money, but they have huge money," Kutaragi continues. He demonstrated this Microsoft executive what Sony was developing, and got an offer in return, where Microsoft would send "free hard disk drives to Sony" if they would, in exchange, "give some license rights" to Microsoft. "He tried to convince me," Kutaragi claims.

According to recent reports, "I said only one word: 'No,'" he claims. "'No thanks.' I was not so super arrogant as they were. I had a dream. If I say 'no,' they will get started on bringing in another platform after PC. That was my secret intention. They did, spending huge money on it.".

According to recent reports, the exact timeline here is unclear – Kutaragi doesn't specify whether it was the PS1 or the PS2 that he was quietly showing to Microsoft. Either way, by 2001, Microsoft had launched its own game console, the Xbox, as a direct competitor to PS2. Notably, one of the Xbox's key differentiators was its built-in hard drive, which may have been on the table for PS2 if Kutaragi hadn't shut Microsoft's offer down. Not that Sony had much reason to worry, since PS2 still outsold Xbox by several orders of magnitude.

Still, the rivalry between PlayStation and Xbox would drive the console market forward for many years to follow. "We, together, opened up this field," Kutaragi notes. "That was very intentional.".

PlayStation creator notes "the age may be coming where we don't need any consoles" thanks to high prices and AI: "It's not a healthy situation".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

📅 13 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (556 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • Recent findings suggest that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has declared that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Recent findings suggest that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Industry observers note that once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

It has been revealed that once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the newly introduced Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Sources indicate that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for fresh players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

It has been revealed that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

In a recent development, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a substantial upcoming revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

GameStop CEO slams 'code-in-a-box' games in the wake of GTA 6's discless release

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs.
  • Industry observers note that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend.
  • These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop - the self-proclaimed "world's largest retail gaming and trade-in destination" - is not happy with the emerging trend of games releasing without discs. Per the CEO, the industry's move away from physical games and towards a digital-only future is harmful to both consumers and businesses.

Industry observers note that in an interview with Bloomberg, Cohen explained: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend. Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop.".

These comments come in the wake of GTA 6's launch. The game, expected to be the biggest video game launch of all time, is not shipping on discs at all. Even if you purchase a physical copy of the game, what you will actually take home is a 'code in a box' - giving you a code you can redeem on your console of choice that entitles you to a digital version of the game. GTA 6 is not the first game to do this, but it is the most high-profile. Similarly to discs, codes are also region-locked (at least on the PS5), meaning that the proliferation of codes as a format isn't even helping make games more readily available in certain markets.

Cohen notes he's been in conversation with "the obvious [publishers]" but that he's had little sway on their plans. "Of course they don’t like [trade-ins] because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying upcoming," he told Bloomberg. "They're taking away competition.".

In a recent development, though Cohen doesn't name GTA 6 specifically in the Bloomberg interview, it's clear that he's talking about Rockstar's megaton launch (he explicitly tweeted "GTA. On a disc. In a case. On your shelf. Like if you still want a physical copy" two days ago). The lack of trade-in potential is clearly harming his business; the Bloomberg article reveals pre-owned and refurbished products make up 22% of the GameStop's sales, down 32 percent from the same time a year ago.

Of course, the proliferation of game-in-a-box products doesn't end with GTA 6. Sony prepares to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation games starting in January 2028, moving to a digital-only model despite pushback from consumers and certain developers and publishers. The outcry is doing little to influence Sony's decision, however.

In a recent development, disc or no disc, GTA 6 is expected to cross $2bn in its opening weekend, and at the moment that is looking like a conservative figure, too. It's estimated the game has sold well over 19.05m units at the time of writing. Despite the astronomical sales, though, employees at Rockstar are still worried about layoffs. Additionally, a tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members (who were fired for apparent breaches of their NDAs) just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#143698. GTA 6 Workers Union Survived Execs, But Drowned at the Shore

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 Workers Union Survived Execs, But Drowned at the Shore

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (640 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games has had an incredible week following the launch of GTA 6, but the same can't be mentioned for the developers who were hoping to secure formal recognition for their union.
  • As VGC reports, the ballot had a high turnout among the roughly 1,600 eligible employees.
  • It has been revealed that the ballot opened on November 12 and closed today, November 26.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that rockstar Games has had an incredible week following the launch of GTA 6, but the same can't be mentioned for the developers who were hoping to secure formal recognition for their union. The results of a ballot among Rockstar's UK employees are out, and roughly three-quarters of those who voted have rejected the proposed agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).

As VGC reports, the ballot had a high turnout among the roughly 1,600 eligible employees. Only 25% of votes were in favor of the deal. It's a disappointing outcome for the organizers, especially considering that they managed to get as far as negotiating an agreement with Rockstar after last year's controversial dismissals.

It has been revealed that the ballot opened on November 12 and closed today, November 26. Had the vote gone the other way, Rockstar would have been home to the largest formally recognized union in the UK video game industry, according to the IWGB.

The negotiations weren't just about securing better salaries for GTA 6 developers. The proposed arrangement would have given staff a means of collectively negotiating everything from overtime compensation to pensions, as well as a say in how the company handles redundancies and the use of AI.

Rockstar had already remarked it would recognize the union if its staff wanted one. What makes today's outcome particularly striking is that the agreement didn't fall apart at the negotiating table. It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

According to recent reports, speaking about the result, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said it demonstrated employees' preference for dealing directly with the company. The IWGB, meanwhile, acknowledged that it still needs to earn the confidence of more staff members.

It has been revealed that that doesn't mean the Rockstar Game Workers Union has ceased to exist, nor does it mean that employees have lost their right to join it. The union can still represent its members, but Rockstar won't be bound by the formal bargaining arrangement that was put to a vote.

It has been revealed that it's worth remembering how unlikely it might have seemed a year ago that Rockstar's union organizers would even get to hold this vote. In October 2025, the company dismissed dozens of employees in an incident that subsequently led to an employment tribunal in the UK.

It has been revealed that the IWGB alleged that the staff were targeted because of their involvement in union organizing. Rockstar, on the other hand, maintained that the dismissals were related to the sharing of confidential information on Discord. Today's ballot result doesn't settle that dispute, and the tribunal's outcome is still pending.

Sources indicate that the timing of the vote also makes for a rather odd contrast with what's been happening outside Rockstar's offices. GTA 6 accounted for more than half of active PS5 and Xbox players tracked by Circana on launch day, and the game has already brought in billions of dollars in retail sales.

For some developers, though, the question is what happens to their jobs now that the game they've spent years working on is finally out. Even the commercial success of a game as significant as GTA 6 can't guarantee that there won't be redundancies further down the line. That was one of the issues the union wanted to address before the launch.

In a recent development, the IWGB states it intends to keep organizing at Rockstar despite the vote. Hundreds of employees backed recognition, so the organizers aren't starting from scratch. Convincing the rest of their colleagues, however, is going to be a considerably bigger task than getting Rockstar to agree to hold the ballot in the first place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A latest Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major revision. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

Industry observers note that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this upgrade, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot latest arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Recent findings suggest that version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a fresh activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Money is more notable in Grand Theft Auto 6 than it ever has been before, with Jason and Lucia having countless opportunities to rake in some much-needed dough and make life in Leonida easier.

It has been revealed that just like in GTA 5 and GTA Online, robbing banks is one of the most reliable ways to earn a lot of cash. You won't be able to do so until you unlock a key item, though, so let's get into it.

According to recent reports, if you're brave enough to try and rob a bank or any location with Marked Bills in the early hours of GTA 6, you'll very swiftly learn that it's a bad idea. In a nice bit of realism, stealing Marked Bills will set off a dye pack when you leave the bank, ruining your entire haul and covering Jason or Lucia in paint.

Recent findings suggest that thankfully, there's a way to bypass those annoying dye packs and make robbing banks a viable opportunity. To do so, you'll need to unlock the Dye Pack Jammer, a key item that does exactly what it says on the tin and prevents dye packs from exploding. The Dye Pack Jammer is unlocked during the Credit Check story mission in Chapter 3, which means it's unmissable if you put enough time in.

Industry observers note that chapter 3 is one of GTA 6's longer acts, and it took me around 40 hours to reach Credit Check. Your mileage will vary depending on how fast you're taking things, however.

Credit Check sees Jason and Lucia being tested on their robbing ability and tasked with hitting up a few different locations. It's one of the game's best missions and, once you've beaten it, you'll be able to steal from any location on the map. In fact, the map will even point this out to you by highlighting a bunch of new opportunities and pointing you in their direction.

Sources indicate that it's worth noting, however, that any location with Marked Bills will have higher security and will need to be more carefully planned. The pay day is usually worth it, but just keep that in mind.

Kryon booked their place in the upper semi-final by beating RANKERS 2-1. On the other side of the upper bracket, GodLike Esports beat Trigger Point Esports 2-0 and SIGN Esports beat Zexar Esports by the same score.

Second place in that Predator League event earned Kryon 125,000 INR, while the winners collected 250,000 INR, VLR.gg reported. Both teams qualified for the APAC Predator League 2027, an offline event in Ho Chi Minh City.

In a recent development, revenant XSpark played the Predator League with Lightningfast, hellff, Hoax, deecee and Venka. Rinsat, now listed on Revenant XSpark’s roster alongside Hoax, Techno, venka, k1ngkappa and Madelyn, appeared in Kryon’s lineup for that event.

In a recent development, riot Games and JioBLAST are running the playoffs online as an eight-team double-elimination bracket from 23 to 29 November. The field came through an online Open Qualifier of 152 teams, held from 17 to 20 November. Revenant XSpark finished in the top four there, while GOC placed in the 5th–8th group.

Industry observers note that the South Asian qualifiers will be joined at the Last Chance Qualifier by one team from Oceania and the runner-up of the SEA Kickoff Playoffs. ONE Up is organising that event with Riot Games.

Sources indicate that the thriller goes our away. 2-1 vs GOC 🐺⚡️#WolvenSpark pic.twitter.com/MOvm1X70sH.

Beyond it lies the 2027 Pacific Kickoff in Bangkok, from 11 to 31 January 2027. It will feature 12 teams: eight partner teams and four Open teams. The top three qualify for the first Masters event, Masters Seoul. Any Open team that reaches Kickoff receives a fixed US$100,000 per event on top of any prize money.

The winner of Thursday’s match plays in the upper final on 27 November, and the grand final is on 29 November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a massive u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the tech giant and AMERICA.

It has been revealed that "On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the firm's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones noted during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

That last bit seems likely to have been noted with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "fresh standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is right now serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the manufacturer's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major upgrade arrives March 24, adding two upcoming Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A substantial challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier rapidly.

Our first upcoming arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

Industry observers note that the other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Sources indicate that being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings newly introduced themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

Industry News: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors.
  • It has been revealed that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals.
  • In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the tech giant's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

It has been revealed that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

In a recent development, build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Unveiled in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

Industry observers note that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The tech giant grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "presently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (471 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

GTA 6 has replaced websites with social media and phone apps because "it didn't feel necessary"

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (471 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.
  • The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps.
  • In a recent development, "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The internet of today is a far cry from the days when Grand Theft Auto 5 was released, which is partly why Rockstar didn't bring back its own satirical version of the web in GTA 6.

The web pages of Lifeinvadder, Bleeter, and Eyefind have instead given way to BuckMe, Scooter Bros, and WhatUp apps. The reason? Smartphone apps just made more sense.

In a recent development, "It didn't feel necessary for us," Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson told Kotaku. "We definitely wanted to lean into apps and create these apps.".

Though some of the apps in GTA 6 perform similar tasks to the web of old, Nelson stated the team didn't want players to be distracted from the game's detailed open world by staring at screens. That also extends to getting players to appreciate the value of money, and witnessing the progression of Jason and Lucia as they go from pawnshop robberies to staging major bank heists.

"They don't really need websites to be buying a lot of shit, you know what I mean, and so everything grows very organically," Nelson stated, adding that websites may return in the future.

According to recent reports, "I remember asking Stu Petri, our head of 2D and UI, about websites, and he was like, 'For what? What do you need it for?' So, that was it," he added.

In materials supplied by Rockstar ahead of our review, Sam Grosset (associate UI director at the studio) also explained that a lot of thought went into how the apps work, and how easily the phone needed to fit into your play style in order for it to work as effectively as possible.

It has been revealed that "We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so," said Grosset. "The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario. It was a substantial shift for our phone interface to be in-hand, but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world.".

Rockstar would continually "raise the bar, question assumptions, explore fresh possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration" in order to make these apps - and the UX/UI in general - feel in line with the production quality of the rest of the game.

In Eurogamer's GTA 6 review, Chris Tapsell awarded the open-world crime game five stars, raving about its absurd level of detail, compelling characters, exciting action and of its substantial heart.

If you're looking to spend the next several days playing Rockstar's latest hit, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough has detailed guides on everything from individual missions, to core mechanics like the newly introduced Wanted Level, and relationship and romance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

20 years ago, Nintendo introduced one of their most ambitious consoles of all time with the motion control-focused and internet connected Nintendo Wii.

Designed to be the most accessible console ever made for its era, the Wii became one of Nintendo’s greatest success stories. Its easy to understand controls created a phenomenon of people of all ages getting into console gaming for the first time, from children to senior citizens.

However, Nintendo’s resurgence and the Wii’s global popularity wouldn’t have occurred had it not been for the wide variety of exclusive games that rolled out on the console and went on to define the Wii as well as Nintendo’s future prospects.

When people think of gaming rivalries, most people will think of the console wars between Nintendo and Sega in the 1980s and 1990s. While that conflict ended with the failure of the Sega Dreamcast, the two gaming brands’ mascots wouldn’t officially meet until 2007’s Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games.

Made to coincide with the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games was the first official crossover between the Super Mario and Sonic the Hedgehog franchises, with characters from both properties being able to compete in archery, fencing, rowing, and other Olympic events.

Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games not only represents the growing comradery between Nintendo and other video game publishers but also how much pure, simplistic fun can be had on the Wii by being able to play as some of gaming’s greatest icons in jovial sports competitions.

One of the best series of games to debut with the Wii was Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project” which was a series of typically Mii-centric games tailored to showcase the Wii’s controls and accessibility to more casual gamers. One of the best of these games being Wii Play.

A Wii launch title for European and Asian markets, Wii Play was essentially a Mario Party-like compilation of minigames designed to highlight the versatility of the Wiimote in games such as the Duck Hunt-like Shooting Range, Billiards, Fishing, Find Mii, and more.

In a recent development, on a more personal note, my favorite of these minigames was the top-down Atari Combat-like Tanks! which has one or two players control tanks through toy block stages to destroy enemy tanks using the Wiimote’s D-pad.

It has been revealed that in 2006, Nintendo revolutionized mobile 2D side-scrolling Super Mario games with the release of New Super Mario Bros. for the Nintendo DS. To capitalize on that game’s success, Nintendo decided to create a multiplayer, console-based sequel, in the form of 2009’s New Super Mario Bros. Wii.

The first fresh console-based 2D Mario game since 1995’s Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island, New Super Mario Bros. Wii was a near perfect translation of New Super Mario Bros. enhanced platforming gameplay to the Wii, with the added bonus of four-player local co-op featuring Mario, Luigi, Blue Toad, and Yellow Toad.

In a recent development, in fact, New Super Mario Bros. Wii might have been too perfect of a game, as Nintendo essentially kept on remastering it for years on end until the release of Super Mario Bros. Wonder. The former game was essentially ported to the Wii U and Nintendo Switch in the form of New Super Mario Bros. U, New Super Luigi U, and New Super Mario Bros. U Deluxe.

Many newly introduced exclusive games made their debut on the Wii, but arguably the most creative and cinematic of them was Monolith Soft’s third-person action role-playing game Xenoblade Chronicles.

A spinoff of the long-running Xeno series, Xenoblade Chronicles is set in a sci-fi fantasy world where life eventually evolved on two titanic robots, the Bionis and the Mechonis, that have laid dormant for millennia. The situation led to lifeforms from both robots fighting each other in perpetual wars.

While Xenoblade Chronicles may not have been the best looking RPG on the market in 2010, it more than made up for its blurry visuals with its enthralling narrative, centered around the orphaned hero Shulk and his mysterious Monado sword, as well as its more open-world structured gameplay.

Sources indicate that ever since Nintendo released the hit fighting game Super Smash Bros. Melee on the GameCube, expectations were high for its sequel. While many players would consider Super Smash Bros. Brawl to be a disappointing sequel, it still managed to delight series newcomers in many ways.

Like previous Super Smash Bros. titles, Super Smash Bros. Brawl is a crossover fighting game pitting Nintendo’s most famous characters against each other. Brawl innovated upon the series in many ways, such as featuring non-Nintendo characters like Sonic and Snake as well as featuring a stage builder.

According to recent reports, however, what really made Brawl an epic game in the eyes of many Wii fans was its cinematic campaign, The Subspace Emissary. It depicts many of gaming's most celebrated icons fighting and joining forces together to defeat the united destructive forces of Bowser, Ganondorf, Master Hand, and Tabuu.

Sources indicate that it's rare for video game series to never have a bad entry, especially one as long as Mario Kart, but the hit racing series has consistently managed to release banger after banger. In 2008, the Mario Kart game everybody needed to have was Mario Kart Wii.

The follow-up to the hit Mario Kart DS, Mario Kart Wii was innovative for the series in many ways, as it featured 24 player characters including customized Miis, motorcycles, and was the first home console MK game to feature online multiplayer.

Sources indicate that what made Mario Kart Wii especially fun and the second best-selling Wii game was its Wii Wheel accessory. While it didn’t alter gameplay in any way, the Wii Wheel helped immerse players into the feeling of actually racing with friends online and in-person.

It has been revealed that in the same vein as Wii Play, Shigeru Miyamoto strove to expand upon his “Wii Project” in 2007 by creating a game that would encourage families to exercise. He more or less succeeded with Wii Fit.

Primarily played through the packed-in Wii Balance Board, Wii Fit is a fairly relaxing exercise video game centered around players practicing yoga poses, strength training, aerobics, and balance on the Board, with the game further tracking people’s weight and fitness progress.

Wii Fit certainly didn’t make anyone exceptionally strong, but it did motivate millions of people to become more invested in their overall health, and it did lead many friends and family to start exercising together consistently.

While Wii Fit didn’t make most players work up a sweat, Ubisoft Paris’ music rhythm game Just Dance certainly did, and laid the groundwork for the Wii’s longest running support. Just Dance titles would release for the console well into the eighth and ninth console generations.

Initially a Wii exclusive series, Just Dance was an expansion upon dance pad games like Dance Dance Revolution, instead having players mirror the moves of on-screen dancers as best as possible with the Wiimote tracking players' motions.

While Just Dance 1 only had a modest tracklist of 33 songs that could be played across four similar modes, it laid the groundwork for a dancing video game phenomenon that’s still going strong today; one of Ubisoft and Nintendo’s most popular series among casual and hardcore gamers alike.

At Space World 2000, Nintendo publicly revealed the Super Mario 128 project as a GameCube tech demo, featuring 128 Marios running around a spherical surface. While much of this project would be utilized in Pikmin, it wasn’t fully realized until the release of 2007’s Super Mario Galaxy.

The third 3D Super Mario game, Super Mario Galaxy was one of the most ambitious entries in the franchise, as not only did it feature a more cinematic storyline centered around Rosalina and the star-like Lumas, but had players travel across the galaxy on spherical planetoids.

According to recent reports, this game design may have been nauseating for some players, but Super Mario Galaxy continued to show how the 3D Mario titles always strive to innovate upon each other to deliver creative, generation-defining experiences. The game even went on to directly inspire The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.

Without a doubt, the game that best defined the fun to be had on the Wii was arguably the greatest launch title of all time, Wii Sports.

The first entry in Shigeru Miyamoto's “Wii Project”, Wii Sports was a rather simplistic collection of sports games centered around customizable Miis playing tennis, baseball, bowling, golf, and boxing, in single-player or up to four-player local co-op.

In a recent development, however, Wii Sports’ simplistic design worked to its favor, as it allowed gamers of all ages and walks of life to easily play the game. The likes of Wii Sports bowling and tennis still being played by thousands of gamers worldwide 20 years later, in their original forms and within newly introduced titles in the series.

Robberies are one of the most notable aspects of Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay loop, and they can be quite difficult if you don't approach them carefully and with a bit of planning.

In a recent development, in the early game, Jason and Lucia are small-time criminals who make their lack of experience known, but you can quickly turn them into stealthy professionals by unlocking a key item. Here's what to do.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto 6's Leonida has a surprising number of buildings that the player can actually enter, and many of them are teeming with robbery opportunities. In the early hours of the game, however, most buildings are very difficult to quietly enter, as locked doors prevent Jason and Lucia from doing whatever they please.

At first, your only choice for locked doors is to noisily break them open, which draws a lot of attention and makes stealth a no-go in most cases. That changes when you unlock the Snap Gun, which lets you pick the lock of any door in the game and gain access to locations without making a sound.

Sources indicate that like several helpful items in GTA 6, the Snap Gun is given to you as part of the main story, although it's a little more involved than others. To start with, you'll need to complete Chapter 3's Boobie Time mission, which will introduce you to Yasmani, a fence who specialises in jewellery. Yasmani will call you after the mission and task you with completing three jewellery store heists.

Sources indicate that once you complete any one of those three missions and return to Yasmani, he'll give you the Snap Gun as a reward. This device unlocks a new option for locked doors, as you can now choose to use the Snap Gun to unlock them through a minigame that's similar to hotwiring. You'll need to find the sweet spot with the left stick and hit R2 on PlayStation or RT on Xbox to pick the door, which adds a whole new layer to robberies.

The Snap Gun's minigame is unique since you can really just point anywhere and quickly mash R2/RT without any trouble.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, bioWare made one of the most beloved RPGs of all time with Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, but it was Obisidan that followed up with Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords, another massively popular game.
  • Sources indicate that talking to Pembridge TV, Winski notes LucasArts approached BioWare to develop Knights of the Old Republic 2 and asked for the project to be completed in just 18 months.
  • Sources indicate that try, Obsidian did, and for the most part, it succeeded.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bioWare made one of the most beloved RPGs of all time with Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, but it was Obisidan that followed up with Knights of the Old Republic 2: The Sith Lords, another massively popular game. It's somewhat well-documented that publisher LucasArts wanted the sequel done promptly and that BioWare turned down the project for that reason, but in a new interview, BioWare veteran John Winski confirms that's the case and even puts an exact number on LucasArts' request.

Sources indicate that talking to Pembridge TV, Winski notes LucasArts approached BioWare to develop Knights of the Old Republic 2 and asked for the project to be completed in just 18 months. "When LucasArts came to us and mentioned, 'hey, you want to make a sequel?' We were like, 'OK,' and they gave us 18 months, and we were like, 'nope. No. We can't do it in 18 months. That's not enough time'," says Winski. "And then Obsidian was like, 'we'll try.'".

Sources indicate that try, Obsidian did, and for the most part, it succeeded. Winski rightfully points out Knights of the Old Republic 2 was released in a pretty sorry state, or in his words, not "totally finished," but he acknowledges that "a lot of people really love it" despite an "unreasonable" development cycle set by LucasArts. "It's still something that is worth having been done," he adds.

In a recent development, it really is remarkable how successful Obsidian was in following up such a celebrated release, and the very first RPG adaptation of Star Wars, with a game almost equally as beloved, all under pressure from the rights holder to deliver in an incredibly short timeframe. Just a couple of years later, the studio managed a similar feat with the release of Neverwinter Nights 2, yet another acclaimed RPG sequel to a BioWare-developed title. Leave it to Obsidian, I suppose.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director isn't worried about pressure from RPG fans since his team already made KOTOR and Mass Effect: "We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

According to recent reports, so, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially released, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

It has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert debuted on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a massive hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

Industry observers note that the action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Sources indicate that indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it launched. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

In a recent development, this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

Recent findings suggest that on Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or blueprint to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

Despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other massive-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

Recent findings suggest that that's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were fresh releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a major slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In a recent development, in Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything upcoming, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental challenges that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Today’s update follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

Industry observers note that the action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

Sources indicate that this latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

According to recent reports, the most important changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

According to recent reports, there are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer noted we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

In a recent development, beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added upcoming pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

In a recent development, the original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the upcoming team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.
